title: Sit with Shiva
line: For stillness, for beginning again, for letting what is finished end.
intro: Shiva is stillness itself: the one who sits unmoved while everything changes, and who ends what needs to end so something new can begin. This practice is a few minutes of sitting with that stillness.
offering: Water, a bilva leaf, or simply your attention.

steps.title: Arrive
steps.text: Sit comfortably, with your back upright and soft. Follow the circle: in as it grows, out as it settles. Never strain.

steps.title: Light the lamp
steps.text: Light a real diya if you have one, or this one. Let the flame be the centre of your attention for a moment.

steps.title: Invoke him
steps.text: Read this verse once, slowly. It sees Shiva as pure as camphor, compassionate, dwelling in the lotus of the heart with Bhavani.

steps.title: The five syllables
steps.text: Repeat AUM Namah Shivaya, gently, as many times as feels true. Let each repetition land in the stillness after it.

steps.title: Be still
steps.text: Sit for a moment with this question. You may write a line, or simply let it rest.
steps.prompt: What could I let be still today, instead of fixing it?

steps.title: Close
steps.text: Read the closing prayer once, slowly. Then sit for one more breath before you return to your day.

after: Shiva is honoured especially on Mondays, and on Mahashivaratri. Coming back to these five syllables each day, even a few times, is a practice in itself.
